title: My bathroom mirror started showing me a few seconds late. Tonight my reflection stopped copying me altogether.
transcript:
My bathroom mirror started showing me a few seconds late. Tonight my reflection stopped copying me altogether. It began as a glitch I could explain away. I'd lift my hand to brush my hair and the mirror would lift its hand a second later, like a video call with bad signal.

I told myself I was tired. I was working doubles, sleeping four hours a night, and everyone knows tired eyes see strange things.

Then the delay grew. Three seconds. Five. I'd walk away from the sink and my reflection would still be standing there, finishing its yawn, turning its head to watch me leave.

Last night I stood in front of the mirror and didn't move at all. I held my breath. My reflection kept breathing.

It tilted its head and smiled slowly, the way you smile at someone you have been practicing to be.

I backed out of the bathroom and turned off the light, and in the dark hallway I heard the faucet start running behind me.

I haven't gone back in. But this morning the mirror in my bedroom was empty. Just the bed, the window, the closet.

I was nowhere in it.

Something is brushing my hair in the next room.
